title: Boss: keystroke golf
summary: Four real edits from real error messages, each in as few keys as you can.

steps.title: Fewer keys, more flow
body: Experienced Vim users move in two or three keys where others hold an arrow down. That is not a party trick: fewer keys means you keep your mind on the bug, not on the cursor.

Each level below starts from something you would really see: a compiler error with a line number, a config value, a broken expression. Solve each one, then try again for three stars (at or under par).
| jump to a character on the line | `f`, `t`, `;` to repeat |
| next match of the word under the cursor | `*`, then `n` |
| change to the end of the line | `C` |

steps.title: error: } expected
prompt: The build says a `}` is missing after line 4, the last line of the `for` loop. Add a line `  }` below line 4.
steps.explain: `4G` jumps by line number, which is what every compiler and stack trace gives you. `o` opens the new line already in Insert mode.

steps.title: Matching brackets
prompt: Delete the whole argument list `(a, (b + c), d)` including its parentheses. The inner pair must not confuse you.
steps.explain: `%` counts nesting, so `d%` from the outer `(` deletes to its own `)`, past the inner pair.

steps.title: Lock down permissions
prompt: Change `chmod 755` to `chmod 700` in as few keys as you can.
steps.explain: `f5` lands on the `5`, and `2r0` replaces two characters without ever entering Insert mode. Replace mode (`R`) is the same idea for longer runs.

steps.title: Change the port
prompt: nginx: change `8080` to `9090` without touching anything else on the line.
steps.explain: `f8` finds the first `8`; `cw` changes to the end of the word. `ciw` would work too and does not care where in the word you are.
